pairwise_removal_interaction_audit.name: pairwise_removal_interaction_audit

predictions.depends_on: REDUNDANT class cells f(S), f(S-a), f(S-b), f(S-ab) where b is a token-matched paraphrase of a with exact action-string match and x is held fixed; Phase 0 gate requiring the same rank-1 item a to give >= +15 net in (a,x) vs (x); class CI +/-5 net.
predictions.falsifier: mean I inside [-4,+4] (additive) or I >= +4 (repetition amplification, each copy adds).
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: Removing either copy deletes no information the set still carries, so I collapses to f(S-ab) - f(S) = minus the joint gain, which the Phase 0 gate pins at <= -15; the falsifier needs the reader to respond to copy count rather than content, a mechanism the design plants no arm for, and the 4-net gap between the confirm and falsify bands is inside the stated +/-5 net class CI.
predictions.fix: Add a dose arm that varies the number of copies of an item whose solo gain is verified small (and a partially degraded paraphrase), decoupled from the >= +15 net Phase 0 gate, and widen the falsifier to I >= 0.

predictions.depends_on: CONFLICT cells plus the Phase 2 Shapley subsets (a,x) and (x); Phase 0 gate that the planted wrong item alone harms >= 10 net; threshold expressed as a fraction of f(a,x) - f(x).
predictions.falsifier: I >= -0.25 x [f(a,x) - f(x)], i.e. a keeps more than three quarters of its solo value while the conflicting item is present.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The falsifier is structurally reachable (a sits in slot 1 and can simply be followed, and the Phase 0 floor on f(b,x) leaves room for a to rescue a depressed baseline), but at the gated gain of about 15 net the confirm boundary (-7.5) and the falsify boundary (-3.75) differ by under 4 net, inside the stated +/-5 net class CI, and both are ratios of two separately noisy measured terms.
predictions.fix: Restate the falsifier as an absolute net threshold (e.g. I >= 0) and size the CONFLICT class so the class-mean I carries a CI under 2 net.

predictions.depends_on: COMPLEMENTARY cells with a and b cut so neither fragment alone contains the whole procedure, natural rank-3 item x held fixed, k=0 success 0.54, 800 cells at +/-5 net.
predictions.falsifier: I <= +3 net (no super-additivity).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The prior at 0.54 k=0 success or the fixed natural rank-3 item can complete the missing half, so single-fragment cells can retain most of the gain and drive I toward zero, and unlike the other classes no positive control forces the joint gain, although the 5-net gap between +8 and +3 only just matches the stated +/-5 net CI.

predictions.depends_on: CONTROL cells (natural rank-1 same-type a plus token-matched cross-type b, x fixed), class CI +/-5 net, no-op repeat as noise floor.
predictions.falsifier: |I| >= 8 net (cross-type items interact by distraction).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Distraction by a cross-type item is a real route to the falsifier, but the 4-net equivalence bound is below the stated +/-5 net class CI, so an observed |I| of 8 has a CI that still contains 4 and neither side of the decision can be separated.
predictions.fix: Raise cells or seeds until the CONTROL class CI is about +/-2 net, or pre-register the class as a formal equivalence test with the bound set above the measured CI.

predictions.depends_on: Phase 2 completion of all eight subsets of (a,b,x) for CONFLICT, REDUNDANT and CONTROL under the same seeds; per-set top-item agreement between phi_LOO and exact Shapley, minus the no-op-repeat disagreement rate.
predictions.falsifier: excess top-item disagreement over CONTROL below 5 points.
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: With all eight subsets measured, phi_SH(i) - phi_LOO(i) is a fixed linear function of the same interaction terms P1 to P4 report, and the REDUNDANT construction forces phi_LOO(a) = phi_LOO(b) about 0 while Shapley splits the Phase 0-gated >= 15 net gain between the two copies, so the disagreement excess restates the manufactured redundancy rather than testing the estimator, and the falsifier would require CONTROL disagreement to rise to match it.
predictions.fix: Report the excess separately per class and make the confirmatory claim on natural unmanufactured k=3 sets, keeping REDUNDANT as a construction check only.

predictions.depends_on: 4 seeds per (game, seed) cell; split-half sign agreement of per-set phi_LOO as a function of seed count; no-op repeat flip rate.
predictions.falsifier: 2 seeds already give split-half sign agreement >= 0.9.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: With only 4 seeds per cell a split-half at 4 seeds per half is never measured, so the >= 4 seeds side cannot be evaluated at all, and at 2 seeds per half the statistic is dominated by tied zero-valued LOO cells whose treatment in the sign-agreement rule is left unspecified, so the falsifier can be manufactured or destroyed by that convention.
predictions.fix: Run 8 seeds on a subsample so genuine 4-vs-4 halves exist, and pre-register how zero or tied per-set LOO values count in the sign-agreement statistic.

predictions.depends_on: Phase 4 CONFLICT cells with x replaced by a natural cross-type item (and by the natural rank-2 same-type item), compared against the Phase 1 CONFLICT masking term; each class mean at +/-5 net.
predictions.falsifier: the CONFLICT masking term changes by >= 10 net under the background swap.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: A three-body masking effect is reachable, but the estimand is a difference of two class-mean interaction terms each at +/-5 net, giving roughly +/-7 net on the difference, wider than the 6-net gap between the <= 4 net prediction and the 10-net falsifier.
predictions.fix: Size the background-swap arm so the difference-of-differences CI is under 3 net, or set the falsifier above the propagated CI.

shared_terms: P1-P5: with all eight subsets measured, phi_SH(i) minus phi_LOO(i) is a fixed linear function of the same interaction terms I that P1 reports, so the REDUNDANT interaction value determines the REDUNDANT rank-disagreement rate.
P2-P5: the CONFLICT interaction uses f(a,x) = f(S-b) and f(x) = f(S-ab), the same measured cells that set P2's own threshold and that enter the Shapley values scored in P5.
P2-P7: P7's estimand is the same CONFLICT masking term as P2 recomputed with a different x, so P2's measurement noise propagates into P7 unchanged.

P1-P6 (and P2-P4-P6): split-half sign agreement of per-set LOO is computed from the same per-cell f(S), f(S-a), f(S-b) values that produce every class interaction, so the seed-count estimand inherits the same flip rate it is meant to characterise.

memory_failure_blame_item_vs_set.name: memory_failure_blame_item_vs_set

predictions.depends_on: Harmed-game set (p0 >= 0.75 and p3 <= 0.25 over 4 seeds, split-half stable); single/pair/diffuse taxonomy from the S-i and S-ij cells under the restoration rule p(S-i) >= p0 - 0.25; expected 45 to 105 harmed games.
predictions.falsifier: single-culprit fraction <= 0.4 (pair-culprit or diffuse majority).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Diffuse harm across three items plausibly leaves every single-removal cell below p0 - 0.25 (the rule demands recovery of at least half the harm gap), so the falsifier is reachable and the 0.6-vs-0.4 gap is roughly two CI half-widths at 80 games, although taking the maximum over three 4-seed estimates without multiplicity or no-op correction biases the count toward the prediction.

predictions.depends_on: Culprit labels from the single-removal cells on the harmed games, cross-type share among all k=3 retrieved items from the retrieval logs, cluster-bootstrap odds ratios.
predictions.falsifier: odds ratio <= 1.2 for cross-type items among culprits.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Same-type near-miss items are an equally available culprit class so OR <= 1.2 is reachable, but with roughly 30 to 60 single-culprit items the log-odds SE is about 0.3, so an OR of 2.0 carries a CI of about [1.1, 3.5] that already contains the 1.2 falsifier, and no MDE for the OR is stated anywhere in the design.
predictions.fix: Pre-register the culprit count needed for the stated OR contrast (roughly 150 single-culprit games, or a coarser two-class collapse) and state the OR MDE alongside the harmed-game sizing rule.

predictions.depends_on: Single-culprit cells; action-copy score over actions up to the first deviation from a successful k=0 trajectory after object-id normalisation; position-rank and retrieval-score baselines; paired top-1 accuracy per cell.
predictions.falsifier: action-copy top-1 accuracy <= position-rank + 0.10.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: The proxy is read off behaviour traces while the culprit label comes from removal cells, so a copied-but-harmless item breaks the correspondence and slot-1 blame can match the proxy (chance is 0.33 for three items), and the paired within-cell comparison keeps a 0.25-point gap detectable at the expected 30 to 60 cells, though only just.

predictions.depends_on: Static-procedure (Measurement C) prompt arm on single-culprit harmed games at 4 seeds, scored against the absolute threshold p >= 0.75; harmed games are defined by k=0 success p0 >= 0.75.
predictions.falsifier: the static arm succeeds on <= 40% of single-culprit harmed games (the task type itself is the difficulty).
predictions.label: entailed
predictions.reason: Harmed games are selected for succeeding without memory at p0 >= 0.75, so an arm that is k=0 plus the type's own correct procedure sentence re-describes the selection filter; reaching <= 40% would require that added sentence to destroy success on games already solved without it, and no paired k=0 re-run is run in the same cells that could expose or price that effect.
predictions.fix: Score the static arm as a paired difference against a fresh k=0 re-run on the same new seeds (estimand: static minus k=0 per game) instead of against an absolute p >= 0.75 threshold, so a null or negative type effect can falsify.

predictions.depends_on: Re-embedding arm on single-culprit games with the two non-culprit items replaced by the next two same-type items from the logs; joint criterion p(S'') <= 0.25 and p(S''-culprit) >= p0 - 0.25 at 4 seeds on about 50 games.
predictions.falsifier: transfer holds in <= 30% of re-embedded single-culprit games (harm is a set property).
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Replacing non-culprits with helpful same-type items and regression away from the extreme p3 <= 0.25 selection both push p(S'') above the 0.25 gate, so the falsifier is easily reachable (if anything the design is biased against the prediction), and the 0.6-vs-0.3 gap is about two CI half-widths at 50 games.

predictions.depends_on: Self-pool replicate of discovery on the 274 validation games versus the expert-bank harmed rate, plus diffuse shares from the same taxonomy.
predictions.falsifier: harmed rates within +/-2 points AND diffuse shares within 10 points (a conjunction).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: A harmed rate near 10% on 274 games carries a CI of roughly +/-3.5 points, so the +/-2 point equivalence band lies inside the noise, and because the falsifier is a conjunction any intermediate result (rates 3 points apart, or diffuse shares 12 points apart) resolves the prediction neither way.
predictions.fix: State the falsifier as an upper CI bound on the rate ratio (CI excluding 1.5) on a self-pool sample sized to that MDE, and split the diffuse-share claim into its own separately powered prediction.

predictions.depends_on: The four added seeds (8 total) on harmed games for S and the three S-i cells; split-half culprit agreement as a function of seed count; the p0 - 0.25 restoration rule.
predictions.falsifier: 2 seeds already give split-half culprit agreement >= 0.8.
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: Unlike the seed-count claim in the companion proposal, 8 seeds make a genuine 4-vs-4 split available, and near-deterministic harmed cells (p0 >= 0.75, p3 <= 0.25) could plausibly push 2-seed agreement to 0.8, so both sides are measurable, though how games with no culprit label enter the agreement statistic is unstated.

shared_terms: P1-P2: the culprit set counted by P1 is the numerator of P2's odds ratio, so the p(S-i) >= p0 - 0.25 rule that fixes the single-culprit fraction also fixes which items are eligible for class enrichment.
P1-P3: P3's top-1 accuracy is scored against the culprit labels P1's taxonomy produces on the same removal cells, so a lenient taxonomy moves both estimands together.
P1-P4: the static-arm success rate is computed on exactly the single-culprit games P1 defines and inherits the p0 >= 0.75 selection that defines a harmed game.
P1-P5: P5 reuses the p0 - 0.25 restoration threshold and is evaluated only on the single-culprit games P1 counts, so P1's threshold choice sets P5's base rate.

P1-P7: split-half culprit agreement uses the same per-(game, seed) S and S-i cells and the same restoration rule as the taxonomy, so the reliability estimand is not independent of the fraction it qualifies.

slot_vs_item_credit_permutation.name: slot_vs_item_credit_permutation

predictions.depends_on: ALL-SAME subgroup of the 274 validation games; order cells O, R, ROT plus no-op repeat at 4 seeds; permutation test over run labels; the +/-5 net CI quoted for the full 1,096-cell O/R/ROT set.
predictions.falsifier: |f(R) - f(O)| >= 8 net on ALL-SAME sets (order matters among consistent items).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Primacy or recency acting on consistent content is reachable, but the +/-5 net CI applies to all 274 games while this prediction is scored on the ALL-SAME subgroup alone (size never stated), so the 4-net equivalence bound sits below the noise and an observed 8 net cannot be separated from the predicted <= 4 net.
predictions.fix: Report the ALL-SAME subgroup size and power it (more seeds, or added bank-disjoint train games) to about +/-2 net, and state the null as a formal equivalence test with the bound above the measured CI.

predictions.depends_on: Forced-slot MIXED cells (the single same-type item in slot 1 versus slot 3 with the two cross-type items in fixed relative order), MIXED subgroup at least 120 games x 4 seeds, paired within (game, seed); positive control requiring a MIXED k=3-vs-k=0 gain >= +10 net.
predictions.falsifier: f(slot 1) - f(slot 3) <= +3 net (slot-invariant reader).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: A slot-invariant reader is a live outcome, but 120 games x 4 seeds gives roughly +/-7 net by the proposal's own scaling from 1,096 cells at +/-5 net, wider than the 5-net gap between the +8 prediction and the +3 falsifier, so the pre-registered decision is noise-limited even though a gross null could still be separated from +8.
predictions.fix: Fix the MIXED cell count from the required MDE (about +/-2 net) rather than from whatever the logs happen to yield, or restate the falsifier as a CI whose upper bound excludes +8.

predictions.depends_on: Planted-conflict slot arm on about 140 procedure-type games x 4 seeds with the token-matched wrong-procedure item placed at slot 1, 2 or 3 plus the unplanted natural set; stated +/-6 net on slot contrasts; positive control requiring slot-1 harm >= 10 net.
predictions.falsifier: harm(slot 1) - harm(slot 3) <= 3 net, or harm larger in slot 3 (recency dominance).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Recency dominance is genuinely reachable and its sign would be visible, but the proposal itself states +/-6 net on these slot contrasts, wider than the 5-net gap between its 8-net prediction and its 3-net falsifier, so the pre-registered thresholds are tied to a CI that cannot separate them.
predictions.fix: Add games or seeds until the slot contrast CI is about +/-2 net, or move the falsifier to a difference <= 0 net so only a sign flip counts.

predictions.depends_on: The three planted-slot harm means from the same ~140-game x 4-seed cells against the same unplanted reference.
predictions.falsifier: harm(slot 2) is the minimum (lost-in-the-middle) or the maximum.
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The prediction is an ordering of three means with no magnitude attached, and at the stated +/-6 net per contrast the rank of slot 2 is decided by noise (under a true tie it lands at an extreme two times in three), so the falsifier is not distinguishable from the monotone prediction.
predictions.fix: Pre-register magnitudes (for example harm(2) at least 3 net below harm(1) and at least 3 net above harm(3)) and power those two contrasts explicitly.

predictions.depends_on: k=7 rotation cells moving the rank-1 item to slot 7 versus the original order, MIXED and ALL-SAME, 274 games x 2 seeds x 2 runs plus a repeat.
predictions.falsifier: the MIXED rotation cost is <= 3 net (the primacy premium vanishes with longer context).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: Loss of the premium at longer context is reachable, but this arm runs only 2 seeds and then splits the games into MIXED and ALL-SAME, putting the MIXED contrast CI well above +/-7 net, so both the 8-vs-3 net decision and the paired <= 4 net ALL-SAME bound lie inside the noise.
predictions.fix: Run the k=7 rotation at 4 seeds on MIXED games sized to about +/-3 net before making the MIXED-versus-ALL-SAME comparison.

predictions.depends_on: Nested-k rank-1 credit from the k-sweep logs; content credit f(ROT) - f(ROT minus rank-1); slot component defined as [f(O) - f(O minus rank-1)] minus that content credit; slot-conditional LOO cells (which remove the item from O and from R only); static-procedure arm.
predictions.falsifier: the MIXED slot share is <= 10% of the nested-k rank-1 credit (nested-k credit is content).
predictions.label: unresolvable
predictions.reason: The share is a ratio whose numerator is a difference of two LOO estimates each at +/-5 to +/-7 net over a denominator of the same magnitude, so 30% versus 10% is not separable and no CI for the ratio is stated; the cell f(ROT minus rank-1) is also absent from the experiment list (step 3 removes the item from O and from R), so the two halves of the decomposition would come from differently ordered residual pairs.
predictions.fix: Add the ROT-minus-rank-1 cell so content and slot credit are measured in matched orders, and report the slot component as an absolute net difference with a CI rather than a share of a noisy denominator.

shared_terms: P2-P6: the MIXED slot component is [f(O) - f(O minus rank-1)] minus [f(ROT) - f(ROT minus rank-1)], built from the same forced-slot and rotation cells as P2, so a confirmed P2 mechanically produces a large P6 slot share and a null P2 forces a small one.
P1-P6: the ALL-SAME order null and P6's <= 10% ALL-SAME slot share are computed from the same f(O) and f(R)/f(ROT) cells, so one determines the other up to the LOO denominator.
P3-P4: harm(slot 1), harm(slot 2) and harm(slot 3) are the same three planted-slot means against the same unplanted reference, so P4's ordering claim is fixed by the two quantities P3 contrasts.

P2-P5: the k=7 rotation re-tests the same MIXED classification and the same rank-1 item content as P2 at a longer context, so it shares the MIXED subgroup and its selection rather than being an independent estimand.
